recap.workouts:
CrossFit, 06:08, 86 min, avg HR 110 / max 154, RPE 5, load 25. Clean and jerk built to 195 lb for a 20 lb PR. Kono scaled exactly as called — 95 lb only and a 20 inch box for step-overs, not jump-overs. An hour and a half averaging 110 bpm is cruising, which is what the metcon was supposed to be.

Hypertrophy — upper push + triceps: incline DB press 65 x 12/12/12, dumbbell flys 20 x 15/15, lateral raise 20 x 20/18/18, triceps pushdown 90 x 10/10/9. Two equipment notes logged and not carried forward: the fly was a dumbbell substitution for today only, and the pushdown handle changed, so 90 lb is the new baseline for that movement rather than a drop from 150.

CMI1 — 120:54, 69.3 km, 172 W average, HR 141 avg / 163 max, load 128, paired to the planned session at 93.4% compliance. The structure came out of the file exactly as it was written: 20' warm-up, 2 x (20' threshold / 15' Z1), then 10 x (1' Z4 / 2' Z1).

Warm-up: 20' at 133 W, HR 131 going into block 1.

Block 1 — 20:00 at 225 W, power variation 0.3%. That is the low half of Zone 3 (222–235) to the watt, which is what the plan asked for on a new anchor. HR settled at 142 after the first minute, finished at 156, mean 153, peak 161. Slope +0.6 bpm/min, decoupling 3.6%. HR plateaued clearly under LTHR 159 — the exact condition the plan set for riding block 2 firmer.

Recovery: 15.7' at 128 W.

Block 2 — 20:00 at 235 W. You took the escalation. HR settled 148, finished 161, mean 159, peak 163. Slope +0.4 bpm/min, decoupling 2.3%. Total time above 162 bpm across the whole ride: 2 seconds — that is the sip spike you flagged, and it is exactly as small as you thought.

Then 14.9' at 135 W into the Z4 set.

Z4 — all ten reps, no gate trips. Rep powers: 263, 265, 265, 265, 265, 265, 265, 265, 265, 265 W against a 248–283 band. Recoveries averaged 116 W, which is the low-end Zone 1 you said you were holding on purpose, and HR came back to 127–132 before every single rep. HR peaks only 152–154 — on 1' reps HR lags by design, so the watts are the target that matters there and you hit all ten.

Zone time for the session: 40.1 min Zone 3, 9.8 min Zone 4, Zone X 0.0 min.
recap.takeaways:
1) Endurance verdict — this is the best threshold session of the block, and the reason is block 2. You rode it 10 W harder than block 1 and it decoupled LESS: 2.3% against 3.6%, with a flatter HR slope (+0.4 vs +0.6 bpm/min). Harder work, better coupling, is the signal you want. Block 2 sat at mean HR 159 while holding 235 W — that is exactly bike LTHR at 99.6% of the 236 W anchor. The CT31 tune said FTP 236; today the field agreed with it independently. Confidence: high, read off the full per-second stream.

2) Zero minutes of Zone X across 121 minutes, and ten Z4 reps that never wobbled off 265 W. Week 8 missed 80/20 on 24.9 minutes of Zone X; three days into week 9 you have contributed none of it. The recoveries at 116 W are the reason the tenth rep looked like the first — that was a deliberate choice and it paid.

3) The clean and jerk. 195 lb is a real PR and I am not going to pretend I am unhappy about it. But the call was cap at ~85% and stop early, specifically so CMI1 would land — and it landed anyway, so today cost you nothing. Take it as a good afternoon rather than a green light: Friday stacks heavy front squats, wall balls and 4 x 6' at threshold pace, and that is the day the cap actually has teeth.

4) Lifting bookkeeping. Incline DB press topped the range on all three sets at 65 — trigger cleared, 70 lb next push day. Lateral raise gave 20/18/18, so top-of-range-on-all-sets is not met and 20 lb holds; that is the rule applied honestly, not a stall. ADAPT: no-op — all three of today's sessions classified EXECUTED, nothing in the remaining week moves.
recap.tomorrow:
Thu 6 — the whole job is clearing today. No lifting.

06:00 Rogers (AMRAP 30): 400 m run + 8 muscle-ups + 500/450 m row + 15 DB bench 50/35. Scale it to a volume you can hold at a conversational pace for the full 30 — cut the muscle-ups to a number that stays near-unbroken, or sub jumping/banded, jog the 400s honestly slow, steady on the row. If you race this, the afternoon spin cannot do its job and Friday's threshold run inherits the debt.

Endurance — CRe10: 75' pure Zone 1 at 118–165 W. No Zone 2 creep, no it-felt-easy-so-I-lifted-it. Being boring is the entire value.

recapPrev.workouts:
Three pieces today, and the one that mattered was executed properly.

06:00 Cutthroat — 56' gym block, avg HR 112, max 151, load 20, RPE 5. You took 135 lb on the clean and jerks and normal wall walks rather than the light-bar [FITNESS] version I called for, plus the 60 single unders per round. Honest flag: on the lowest readiness morning of the block, that was the version with the most room to go wrong. It didn't — avg HR 112 and max 151 say you genuinely cruised it, and 21 total C&J reps at 135 sits well inside your strength. Noted, not scolded.

Arms and delts, the full Friday dose at exactly the deload loads: triceps pushdown 135 × 13, barbell curl 40 × 12, lateral raise 20 × 20. You were right about the Sorinex station — those are hamstring curls, so substituting your own barbell curls was the correct read, and the class banded face pulls covered the rear delts.

RAn4 — 45:03, 7.27 km, load 37 against a planned 45, RPE 5, paired cleanly to the planned session. The file splits exactly to the prescription: 15:01 warm-up, then 4 × (2:30 hard / 5:00 jog). Nothing missing, nothing added. The 82% compliance figure is intervals.icu scoring against its own preset zones, not a shortfall — every step is there at full length.

Warm-up: 5:56/km, HR 119 avg, max 132. Honest Z1.

The four reps, target band 3:48–4:17/km:
rep 1 — 4:08/km, HR 131 at the gun to 158 by the end
rep 2 — 4:03/km, 120 to 161
rep 3 — 4:08/km, 126 to 162
rep 4 — 4:03/km, 130 to 176

All four inside the band, total spread across the set five seconds per kilometre, and the last rep tied the fastest. That is exactly the shape this session wants: crisp, repeatable, no decay.

The HR story — and this is precisely why interval averages are useless here: rep 2 carries a LOWER average than rep 1 despite being five seconds per km quicker, purely because you started it from 120 instead of 131. Read the peaks instead: 158 · 161 · 162 · 176. The first three climb four beats in total across the set, which is a tightly controlled ladder. Rep 4 jumps 14 beats at exactly rep 2's pace — a slice of that is the 5 m of climbing inside that rep, the rest is you closing the session hard. 176 is the highest heart rate in your file this block, above Thursday's 173, and it sits at the top of the new Z4 band (167–175), so rep 4 is the only rep that reached Zone 4 by heart rate. Reps 1–3 peaked 158–162, i.e. high Z3. On 2.5-minute reps starting from a fully recovered HR that is normal lag, not a soft effort — pace is the sharp target here, and pace was hit every time.

Recoveries: 8:12 · 9:07 · 8:58 · 8:39 per km, HR dropping to 108 · 101 · 113 · 114. You shed 50-plus beats between every rep. On the day the panel called your worst of the block, that is a body still recovering fast.

Method note: analysed off the workout-matched interval table, which maps 1:1 to the prescribed steps (901 s warm-up, then 150 s / 300 s four times). The per-second stream pass wasn't available this evening — the Drive folder didn't mount into the compute sandbox — so pace is per-rep rather than per-second. Nothing above is estimated.
recapPrev.takeaways:
1) The run verdict: clean. Four reps inside the pace band, five seconds per km of spread across the whole set, the last one tied fastest, HR shedding 50+ beats in every recovery, and no drift signal anywhere. Load 37 — a fraction of Thursday. As stimulus maintenance it did exactly its job, and there is no fatigue flag in the trace. Confidence: high on the pace read, medium on the HR read (per-rep peaks rather than per-second plateaus).

2) The call, straight. I recommended cutting RAn4 this morning at readiness 27 and you ran it — second day running that you overrode me and the file came back clean. What I actually think, rather than just conceding: the execution was good, and a load of 37 is not what turns a deload into Week 4 again. But two overrides in two days is a pattern worth naming, and the readiness signal — sleeping HR elevated a fifth straight morning, breathing now flagged too, Form −25.8 — still hasn't been paid for. One well-run session doesn't settle it. Tomorrow is where it gets settled.

3) ADAPT: no-op. RAn4 EXECUTED at full structure, Cutthroat done heavier than called but genuinely easy by HR, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week moves — and on a deload nothing gets added, ever.

4) Lateral raise 20 lb × 20 tops the range: banked, not applied, per the deload rule. Week 9 now opens with lat pulldown to 190, face pull to 85, leg curl to 50, overhead triceps ext up one step, and lateral raise up one step. Five bumps waiting, all earned this week without spending them.
recapPrev.tomorrow:
CAn4 — 90' on the bike: 10' Z1, then 6 × (2:30 Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 5:00 Z1), 30' Zone 2 @ 165–196 W, 5' Z1. Both bands are the post-CT31 numbers (FTP 236 W). No gym, no class — Saturday is bike only.

If readiness is still down in the twenties, either drop it outright or ride only the 30' Z2 tail — six Z4 reps is the single biggest block of hard time left in a week whose entire job was to deload. If you wake up genuinely normal, ride it as written and keep the recoveries as lazy as today's were.

Sunday is full rest either way. That part isn't negotiable.

recovery.bannerTitle: The gate did not trip — CMI1 is ON
recovery.bannerSub: Two of the three illness markers went out overnight. Wrist temperature dropped to 35.87, the lowest in nine days and back under the flag line; respiratory rate fell to 13.6 and is no longer flagged. The illness flag is OFF for the first time since 29 July and readiness is 33, up five and the best since 30 July. Ride it — block 1 at 222–235 W, and the on-bike gate stays exactly as written.
recovery.note: Readiness 33, up five from 28 and the best number since 30 July, and more importantly the shape of the picture changed rather than just the score. The standing gate said CMI1 slides only if this morning still showed elevated sleeping HR, respiratory rate AND wrist temperature. Two of those three cleared overnight: wrist temperature came in at 35.87, the lowest reading in nine nights and comfortably back under the flag line, and respiratory rate at 13.6 pulls the smooth to 13.8 with z −0.9, under the flag threshold for the first time in a week. The illness flag is off. So the gate does not trip, and my recommendation is unambiguous: ride CMI1 today, as written, this afternoon. The one marker still lagging is sleeping HR — 63 last night, 3-night smooth 64.0 against a 57.8 baseline, z −1.7 — so the code still classifies you 'ease off' and I am not going to pretend otherwise. But it improved three beats on the night, it is the slowest-moving marker of the three, and your warmer-bedroom explanation now has the other two markers walking back to baseline alongside it. Sleep helped: 8.22 h in bed, 7.95 h asleep, 15 minutes awake and 106 minutes of deep — the third consolidated night running and by far the most deep sleep of the block. Load: Form −18.1 against −15.8 yesterday, a touch deeper because Henry cost 41 and the jog 25. On Henry — you flagged it yourself as slightly harder than called, and the file agrees: max HR 174, the highest CrossFit reading of the block, against Monday's 156. That money is already spent, so protect the ride now rather than relitigating it — cap the clean and jerk at about 85%, take Kono with step-overs, and get off the floor early. On the bike: block 1 at 222–235 W and set the effort in the first five minutes, one correction and no stair-stepping. If HR plateaus clearly under 159 in block 1, block 2 can go a touch firmer. And the Z4 gate is not decoration — if you cannot get back to Z1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or a rep drops below 248 W, stop the set. Seven good reps is a completed session.

2026-08-03.mind: Yesterday I rode with no number on it and gave away twelve minutes to Zone X, so today the number is 196 and it is a ceiling, not a target — with my body still running warm, holding the bottom of the band is the win, not a compromise.

end.name: CMI1 — THE WEEK'S SESSION (mixed intervals)
end.desc:
20′ Z1 → 2 × (20′ Zone 3 @ 222–248 W / 15′ Z1) → 10 × (1′ Zone 4 @ 248–283 W / 2′ Z1). (Pulled from the live 80/20 library 2 Aug — structure verbatim. The Z4 set comes AFTER the threshold blocks and the workout ends on the last recovery; add 5′ easy to close if you want it.)
Standing gate from Mon 3 Aug — RESOLVED, and it did not trip. The gate required all three markers still elevated this morning. Wrist temperature fell to 35.87 (lowest in nine nights, under the flag line) and respiratory rate to 13.6 (no longer flagged); the illness flag is off. Only sleeping HR is still up. CMI1 runs today, as written.
The two 20′ blocks are the point — the ten Z4 reps are a top-up on already-tired legs and are meant to feel harder than the watts suggest.
40 minutes of Z3 is double anything you have ridden this block and it is your first threshold work on the new 236 W anchor, so target the low half of the band, 222–235 W, on block 1. If HR plateaus clearly under 159, ride block 2 a touch firmer; if HR is at or above 159 by minute 12 of block 1, hold the watts and let it sit there.
Set the effort in the first 5 minutes of each block and stop adjusting — one early correction, never a stair-step (the 28 Jul CT31 lesson).
On-bike gate for the Z4 set: if you cannot get back to Z1 watts inside the 2′ recovery, or rep power falls below 248 W, stop the set and spin out the remainder. Seven good reps is a completed session; ten bad ones is how week 7 ended.
